questions.question: Define race, prejudice, stereotype, discrimination and racism, and explain why race is called a social construct.
questions.expected_answer: Race: grouping by visible features; all humans one species, about 99.9% shared DNA, more variation within groups than between, skin colour adapts to sunlight; social construct with real effects. Prejudice: prejudging attitude. Stereotype: fixed oversimplified idea about a group (even positive ones harmful). Discrimination: unfair action because of group. Racism: belief in superior/inferior races plus prejudice and discrimination; most harmful with power over laws, land, jobs, education.

questions.question: Explain how racist ideas developed and were used to justify slavery, colonialism and other systems.
questions.expected_answer: From 16th century with colonialism and Atlantic slave trade (over 12 million enslaved Africans); racism justified treating people as property. 18th-19th century scientific racism (skull measurement, rankings), social Darwinism justified conquest and the scramble for Africa; Sarah Baartman exhibited (1810, died 1815, returned 2002). Nazi Aryan ideology, Nuremberg Laws, Holocaust; Jim Crow in USA. UNESCO 1950 statement rejected racial ranking, but SA from 1948 legalised racism.

questions.question: Distinguish personal and institutional racism, using apartheid as an example, and explain how racism can be challenged today.
questions.expected_answer: Personal: individual attitudes and actions, open or unconscious. Institutional/structural: built into laws, rules and institutions regardless of individual intent. Apartheid: Population Registration Act 1950 classified everyone, deciding residence, schooling, jobs, marriage, amenities, vote; pencil test; families split; legacy of inequality in wealth, land, schooling; redress measures debated. Xenophobia (2008, 2015). Challenges: Constitution's non-racialism, Section 9, Equality Act 2000 and Equality Courts, SAHRC; individuals question stereotypes, refuse racist jokes, speak up safely, support targets, report; schools; anti-apartheid struggle across all groups; Freedom Charter.
